lessons.story:
In a classroom investigation, pairs sort picture cards into four groups. In the first round, they are told to finish as fast as possible. In the second, they are told to check every card before stopping. Each round uses a different set with the same number of cards.

One pair finishes the first round in forty seconds with five mistakes. Their second round takes seventy seconds with one mistake. Jun calls the first result better because it is faster. His partner asks whether speed alone is the goal.

The class reports both time and errors. They also note that the second set may have been easier or harder, and practice from the first round may have helped. Their results describe what happened under these conditions. A further comparison could vary the order between groups to examine the instructions more fairly.
lessons.title: Fast Sorting, Careful Sorting
